acceptance.item: P5-RT-04-01: After one press of the skip link (or Back), Copy link on T12, T10 and T11 encodes the codec's reading of the bar, not the state shown: another start and relation, a bare link, or a link that cannot be read
acceptance.test: site/tests/unit/history-popstate-copy-link.test.ts > Copy link after a popstate on a T12 instance opened from a link > <query>: linkFor encodes the state T12 shows, before and after popstate; site/tests/e2e/history-popstate.spec.ts > <route>?<query>: after the skip link, Copy link still encodes the state shown, and > <route>?<query>: after the skip link, the export footer links to the state shown; site/tests/e2e/history-popstate-sweep.spec.ts > <route>?<query>: Copy link is the same before and after the skip link
acceptance.evidence: Severity major (the lens's level; neither verifier adjusted it). Red at base 0be3c0e: unit 'Tests 4 failed (4)' with the verifier's values (?g=E7 Received ...s=1,1,1,1,1,1,1&w=); browser on the base build 14 failed, 11 passed: the 5 sweep failures and 5 T12 failures the verifier saw, plus my 3 export-footer cases on T12, T11 and T10 (same wrong links in the SVG footer); the 11 plain-codec routes passed. Cause: onPopState_ in site/src/lib/history.ts set entry.current to decodeState's reading before calling the tool's handler, and T10 to T12, which admit links by rules of their own, found their state unchanged and reported nothing, so linkFor (Copy link and the export footer) encoded a state not on screen. Fix: the recorded state is no longer replaced; it stays what the tool last reported through stateChanged, and a change that arrives after a popstate before the reader acts again is recorded as that instance's load and not written. Green: unit 23 passed (with history.test.ts unchanged); browser 25 passed, and 41 passed from the clean tree with history-after-action.spec.ts and history-no-write-on-load.spec.ts; engine 2411 passed (baseline 2411). Commit 77292eb.

acceptance.item: P5-RT-04-01 (sibling): the back button rewrote the bar of the entry it returned to on a tool that reads links by its own rules (T12 shown; T10 and T11 share the path)
acceptance.test: site/tests/unit/history-popstate-copy-link.test.ts > the state a popstate loads > T12 back to its link after a move: the state it loads is recorded, not written, and Copy link encodes it; site/tests/e2e/history-popstate.spec.ts > tools/rep/?k=2: back to the link after a move writes nothing, and Copy link encodes the state shown
acceptance.evidence: Same cause. The codec's reading replaced the recorded state, so when T12 loaded its link's state after Back, that state differed from the recorded one and, once the reader had acted, counted as the reader's change and was written. Red at base: unit 'the back button writes nothing: expected length 1 but got 2'; browser Expected '?k=2', Received '?z=1&g=A2&c=n&s=0,1&w=&k=2&q=ef:2,2'. Green after the fix in both. Guard, which passes before and after: 'a tool that reads its links by the codec, on a page opened without a link: back loads, writes nothing, and Copy link encodes the state shown'. Commit 77292eb.

Not fixed, separate cause: a replaceState burst still pending when popstate fires (a move, then Back within 500 ms) is written into the entry the reader returned to, and the entry the reader left keeps its pre-burst URL. With this fix it writes the state shown, not the codec's reading. Cancelling the timer on popstate would be a separate decision.
handoff: Only site/src/lib/history.ts changed (no new export, no signature change). ToolFrame.svelte, T10GeometryStudio.svelte, T11FoldingBench.svelte and T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte needed no edit: their handlers already load what they admit, and ToolFrame's stateChanged effect now records it. So the T12 fixer of the later cluster has nothing of mine to merge around. The proposedFix's two options (ToolFrame records after the handler through a new history.ts function, or the handler returns its state) were not followed: both change an interface (a new export, or a new return type for onPopState), and neither covers loads that finish later (T10's tasks, T11 or T12 worker replay, T8 and T15 async loadLink). The popstate load window, which reuses the phase 4 count of the reader's actions, covers them. The lens should also rerun the back-after-move case and the export footer, now in history-popstate.spec.ts.
